steps.title: Begin with a bound artistic reference
steps.explanation: The poser binds a generated surface to its neutral graph. Vertex identity and triangle connectivity are retained when the rig moves. These geometric contracts describe a render surface, not a volume discretization with material stress.
steps.observe: The neutral surface is visible. Force and pressure remain not modeled even though the object is rendered in three dimensions.

steps.title: Follow the bones through a prescribed bend
steps.explanation: Prescribe the right-hand target from the poser’s existing test case. Dual-quaternion blending moves the surface with the bone transforms; it does not solve the transverse compression, fascia sliding or contact reaction discussed in this chapter.
steps.observe: The right arm and rendered skin change together. This is a geometric pose change, with no reported tissue stress or contact reaction.

steps.title: Make the contact limitation visible
steps.explanation: Cross both arms using the existing two-target pose. Inspect the close surfaces from several angles. A shaded crease is not an intersection test, and retained topology does not guarantee that unrelated surface regions stay apart.
steps.observe: Both arms move into the crossing pose. The example reports contact response as not modeled; it neither certifies separation nor assigns a pressure to apparent contact.

audit.finding: An empty-control poser illustrated skinning without a reproducible bend or contact-limit inspection.
audit.change: Neutral, one-arm bend and crossed-arm presets make the geometric progression reproducible without adding a physical claim.
audit.remaining: No tissue constitutive solve, measured local distortion, contact detection, collision response or pressure field is introduced.
